text: Diagnosis (two archive queries, no screen re-run; raw numbers in diagnosis-counts.json, which the site never reads). (1) Construction: the current catalog rebuilt by the date construction (newest set per object from the by-creation files of the 30 days before the window start, epoch in the last 30 days) holds the same objects as the snapshot-based one: 32,862 shared, 86 only in the rebuild, 1 only in the snapshot (0.3 percent). The date construction and the snapshot do not differ, and the population filter, the set ages (median 0.6 days at 2025-12, 1.3 days now; 90th percentile 2.3 and 2.2 days) and the by-creation coverage are not the cause. (2) Composition: the objects between 400 and 500 km (mean-motion altitude) are 2.16 times as many in the current catalog as at 2025-12-21, those between 500 and 560 km are 0.27 times as many, and the rest of the altitude bands move by under 1.1 times except 600 to 800 km (1.11) and below 400 km (1.05). The construction is not the cause; the composition changed sharply (objects concentrated into a lower, narrower shell); how much of the event jump that carries is not yet measured. It is not a scaling exponent: the dates differ in composition as well as in size, so no fit of events on N across them measures how screening work grows with N. Events by altitude band were not measured (it needs screen runs, held). Until they are, the dates series is not drawn.
